title: Basis of the Assisted Living Returned-Payment Charge by Payer and Amount
content:
The basis of the returned-payment charge on an Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement account follows the instrument and size of the payment returned:

| Payment returned | Basis of the charge |
|---|---|
| A payment from a long-term care insurer | No charge — an insurer transfer reversed by the bank is a processing error and not the household's |
| A household payment of 4000.00 dollars or more | 1.5 percent of the amount returned |
| Any other returned payment | The returned payment fee |

The payment considered is the most recent return reinstated on the residency; its amount is the amount reinstated, and the payer is the payer recorded on the original payment entry that the return reinstated (the long-term care insurer, or the resident or family). The basis is worked out before any other multiplication of the charge and before it is rounded once to the cent.

### Both sides of the threshold (hypothetical household payments)

| Amount returned | Basis |
|---|---|
| 4000.00 | 1.5 percent: 60.00 |
| 3999.99 | The returned payment fee |
| 6250.00 | 1.5 percent: 93.75 |
| 6250.00 paid by the long-term care insurer | No charge |
